answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it can submit work, then slash the bond when a randomly audited task fails or a client proves fraud. A sybil attacker must lock real capital in each fake account, so multiplying identities raises the cost rather than merely changing names. A plume of cheap accounts may cross the bridge into the market, but each must stake funds; even a sonnet-writing bot risks losing its bond when caught cheating.
